 Categories Money Market 8th pay commission salary hike: What central government employees can expect?
 October 31, 2026 by Team Suncrypto 
 AI Summary 
 Lakhs of central government employees and pensioners are waiting for the 8th Pay Commission’s recommendations.
 A Pay Commission is a body set up by the government to review the salary, allowances, and pensions of central government employees.
 The 8th Commission will recommend changes to basic pay, allowances such as HRA and DA, and pensions, and it is expected to review the wider pay structure rather than a single number.
 Basic summary 
 Lakhs of central government employees and pensioners are waiting for the 8th Pay Commission’s recommendations. The commission has been consulting stakeholders across the country, but no final pay figures have been announced. This article explains where things stand, what the fitment factor means, and how a salary revision could affect you.  
 What is the 8th pay commission? 
 A Pay Commission is a body set up by the government to review the salary, allowances, and pensions of central government employees. Commissions have typically been formed roughly every ten years. The government constituted the 8th Central Pay Commission on November 3, 2025, and it is headed by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, with two other members. 
 The 7th Pay Commission set the minimum basic pay at ₹18,000 per month. The 8th Commission will recommend changes to basic pay, allowances such as HRA and DA, and pensions, and it is expected to review the wider pay structure rather than a single number. 
 Latest update on the 8th pay commission salary hike 
 As of October 2026, the government has not announced an approved fitment factor, a revised pay matrix, or a final implementation date. The commission is still in its consultation stage. 
 The commission has scheduled stakeholder meetings in several cities, including Bengaluru in early October and Mumbai on October 22–23, 2026. Confirm the outcome of each visit on official sources before describing it as complete. 
 In a written reply in the Rajya Sabha in July 2026, the government did not give a fitment factor. Any figure circulating online is an estimate, a demand, or an illustration, not an official number. 
 What is the fitment factor? 
 The fitment factor is a multiplier. Your current basic pay is multiplied by it to get your revised basic pay. A higher factor means a bigger increase. 
 The 7th Pay Commission used a factor of 2.57. For the 8th Commission, nothing is final: 
 The commission has said that a figure of 2.1, discussed in some reports, is not final. 
 Some analysts have suggested factors between about 2.28 and 2.86. These are estimates, not forecasts from the commission. 
 Employee federations have submitted higher demands. The National Council of JCM, for example, has proposed a factor of 3.83. 
 How much could your salary go up? 
 The table below applies a few example factors to the 7th Pay Commission’s minimum basic pay of ₹18,000. These are illustrations only, because the real factor is not known.  
 Fitment factor 
 Revised basic pay 
 2.1 
 ₹37,800 
 2.28 
 ₹41,040 
 2.86 
 ₹51,480 
 Keep in mind that basic pay is only one part of take-home salary. Dearness Allowance (DA), HRA, and other allowances are also revised, and the DA rate changes separately, so the overall effect on your salary will differ from the basic pay change alone.  
 Why DA matters? 
 DA is a cost-of-living allowance that is revised periodically. When DA has already risen, a pay commission’s fitment factor needs to be higher to deliver the same real gain. Check the latest DA notification from the government to see your current DA rate before estimating your revised salary.  
 When will the revision take effect? 
 The reference date for revised pay is 1 January 2026. If the revised pay is approved with that effective date but paid later, employees would receive the difference as arrears. 
 Implementation has not been announced. Reports estimate that the final revision will take place in 2027, with arrears from January 2026. Do not plan your budget around an increase that has not been approved. 
 Who is covered? 
 The revision applies to central government employees, including staff in ministries, departments, Railways, and Union Territories. Defense personnel are part of the process, though some provisions may be handled separately. 
 Pensioners are covered too. Pensions and family pensions are normally revised when pay is revised, but the pension formula has not been finalized. 
 The revision does not directly cover: 
 State government employees, whose pay is set by each state. States usually study the central decision and set up their own pay panels. 
 Bank employees, whose pay is negotiated between the Indian Banks’ Association and bank unions. 
 Most private-sector employees, whose pay follows company policy. 
 PSU and autonomous body employees, who should check with their HR department, since coverage can vary. 
 Has the 8th Pay Commission announced its fitment factor?
 No. As of October 2026, the fitment factor, pay matrix, and implementation date have not been announced.
 What was the fitment factor under the 7th Pay Commission?
 It was 2.57, with minimum basic pay set at ₹18,000.
 What will the minimum salary be under the 8th Pay Commission?
 It has not been decided. Any figure you see online is an estimate or a demand.
 When will the 8th Pay Commission be implemented?
 No implementation date has been announced. Reports suggest 2027, with arrears from January 2026, but these are expectations.
 Will pensioners get a hike?
 Pensioners are covered in the process, but the pension formula has not been finalised.
 Who set up the 8th Pay Commission?
 The government constituted it on November 3, 2025, headed by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai.
